papers.title: AnySleep: a channel-agnostic deep learning system for high-resolution sleep staging in multi-center cohorts.
papers.summary: Developed AnySleep, a channel-agnostic deep neural network trained on over 20,000 overnight EEG/EOG recordings from 28 datasets to perform sleep staging at adjustable temporal resolutions. The model achieved state-of-the-art 30-s epoch performance, remained robust with limited channels, and at sub-30-s resolution improved prediction of obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy type 1, and insomnia compared to 30-s scoring.

papers.title: An automated EEG-ECG framework for CAP-HRV analysis: enabling brain-heart coupling studies in sleep disorders.
papers.summary: Presented an open-source MATLAB framework integrating rule-based cyclic alternating pattern (CAP) A1 detection from EEG with heart rate variability (HRV) feature extraction from ECG within a time-synchronized workflow, using validated PhysioZoo/mhrv routines. A worked example on OSAD+ patients (n=18) and a healthy reference dataset (15 controls, 785 A1 epochs) demonstrated synchronized CAP-HRV output to facilitate brain-heart coupling research in sleep disorders.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification in Machine Learning for Biosignal Applications - A Review.
papers.summary: Systematically reviewed 53 papers on uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods for machine learning applied to biosignals such as EEG, ECG, EOG, and EMG. The review catalogued methods, evaluation measures, theoretical frameworks, and misconceptions, concluding that promising UQ approaches exist but that research on human-system interaction with uncertainty models in clinical settings is still needed.

papers.title: Automated attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder detection using an explainable EEGNet model based on electroencephalogram signals.
papers.summary: Developed a lightweight, explainable EEGNet model that processes raw 5-second spatio-temporal EEG segments for automated ADHD detection, achieving 89.48% (±4.21%) average accuracy and AUC 0.96 (±0.03), outperforming transfer learning models. Saliency maps and SHAP values identified key channels (Fp1, Fp2, C3, T5, A2) consistent with ADHD executive dysfunction literature.

papers.title: Decoding Parkinson's disease: a systematic review of qEEG biomarkers across clinical domains.
papers.summary: Systematic review (PRISMA, 89 studies) synthesizing quantitative EEG correlates of Parkinson's disease across cognition, motor function, pharmacology, neuromodulation, and sleep. Spectral slowing (reduced posterior dominant frequency, increased theta) was the most consistent cognitive correlate, while connectivity measures better tracked motor dysfunction, and qEEG changed with dopaminergic drugs and neuromodulation.

papers.title: Interbrain synchrony analysis for fNIRS: A signal processing primer.
papers.summary: Methodological primer on quantifying interbrain synchrony (IBS) in fNIRS hyperscanning studies, explaining time-frequency analysis foundations underlying wavelet transform coherence and its resolution limits. Provides practical recommendations for experiment design, preprocessing, and frequency targeting to improve consistency and reproducibility of IBS measurement.

papers.title: Cortical traveling wave analysis reveals weaker resting forward theta waves and greater task-related modulation in obsessive compulsive disorder.
papers.summary: Compared cortical traveling wave dynamics in 25 OCD patients and 27 controls using resting and task (Go/NoGo, Flanker) EEG, finding weaker resting forward theta traveling waves in OCD and greater task-related forward theta modulation during the Flanker task, with no associations to symptom severity. Findings suggest disrupted hierarchical cortical communication as a potential trait-like marker of OCD.

papers.title: A technical review of dynamic brain functional imaging combined with EEG spectral parameters in the screening of early-stage brain injury.
papers.summary: Technical/narrative review proposing a Dynamic-Spectral Coupling framework linking EEG spectral abnormalities (spectral slowing, 1/f aperiodic components) to dynamic fMRI network disruption for early-stage brain injury screening. Summarizes multimodal fusion technologies for mTBI, occult cerebrovascular injury, and subclinical injury while noting that clinical utility remains to be established.

papers.title: Human iEEG recordings during audiovisual speech violations support and extend predictive routing models
papers.summary: Using human intracranial EEG from seven presurgical epilepsy patients during an audiovisual speech paradigm, the study tested predictive routing predictions by measuring theta, alpha-beta and high-gamma power during auditory deviance, multisensory integration and McGurk incongruence. Superior temporal cortex showed increased high-gamma and decreased alpha-beta power for auditory deviance and McGurk stimuli, whereas frontal areas showed the alpha-beta decrease without a high-gamma prediction error signal and instead a strong theta-band prediction error in the McGurk condition.

papers.title: Differential circadian time modulates of dentate gyrus and CA1 excitation-inhibition balance and seizure threshold.
papers.summary: Using video-EEG, optogenetic seizure induction, mRNA sequencing, and patch-clamp recording in mice, this study showed that circadian time differentially modulates seizure thresholds and excitation-inhibition balance in hippocampal dentate gyrus versus CA1, with CA1 diurnal-nocturnal seizure threshold patterns matching systemic pilocarpine-induced seizures.

papers.title: Hair-compatible adhesive hydrogel electrodes for electroencephalography-based cybersickness detection and closed-loop mitigation.
papers.summary: The authors developed a shell-assisted adhesive hydrogel electrode incorporating PDA/PEDOT particles to achieve conformal, hair-penetrating EEG recording with high conductivity and stability under sweating and motion. The electrode achieved an EEG SNR of 11.66 dB, showed motion interference at 22.8% of that of traditional wet electrodes, and, integrated into a wearable headband, detected cybersickness with 92.5% accuracy and closed-loop nGVS increased tolerance time by 52.3%.

papers.title: Cerebellar Topological Alterations Across the Alzheimer's Disease Continuum.
papers.summary: This EEG study compared 34 healthy controls, 40 MCI patients and 30 Alzheimer's disease patients using phase-locking-value functional connectivity and graph theory to characterize cerebellar-cortical network topology across the AD continuum. Theta-band small-world metrics were reduced in MCI and AD, cerebellar nodal centrality showed an inverted U-shaped relationship with neuropsychological scores, and network-based statistics revealed selective theta-band cerebello-cortical reorganization.

papers.title: A multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset with repeated experience sampling
papers.summary: This paper presents a BIDS-formatted multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset from 24 healthy adults with carbon wire loop artifact sensors, continuous performance task responses, experience sampling of 13 thought dimensions (468 ratings per participant), and mental health surveys across two days (~1.33 hours of simultaneous data per person).

papers.title: Machine Learning Classification of Bipolar Disorder Across Mood States Using Natural Language Processing and Speech Analysis: Observational Study.
papers.summary: This observational study used LASSO-regularized logistic regression on 6373 acoustic and 211 linguistic features from speech samples of 61 bipolar disorder patients and 99 healthy controls to classify bipolar disorder and mood states. The model discriminated bipolar disorder from controls with AUC 0.916 and mood states from controls with AUC 0.805-0.874, with acoustic features comprising 96%-98% of significant features, while depressive vs euthymic state exceeded chance (AUC 0.760) and other interstate comparisons did not.

papers.title: Tetradic Dynamics of Dyadic Sensorimotor Coordination: A Multiscale EEG Hyperscanning Study
papers.summary: This dual-brain EEG hyperscanning study examined leader-follower sensorimotor coordination in healthy adult pairs using a 2x2 design crossing Role with Mirroring versus Matching, proposing a tetradic framework for dyadic interaction. Neural analyses showed greater tonic power and phasic clusters during Matching, role-dependent anticipatory and post-response patterns, and information-theoretic signatures separating Leader-weighted predictive information from Follower-specific adaptive information, with sparse Synergy and Redundancy across specific cortical regions.

papers.title: Neurodynamical heterogeneous spiking neural network for spatiotemporal cognitive signal processing.
papers.summary: The authors propose the Neurodynamical Heterogeneous Spiking Neural Network (NHSNN), which combines LIF, dendrite-inspired Pinsky-Rinzel and leaky resonate-and-fire neuron models in dedicated functional modules for cross-neuronal heterogeneous spike encoding. Evaluated on EEG diagnosis, music classification and textual semantic tasks, NHSNN reached accuracy comparable to mainstream full-precision ANNs on EEG and music benchmarks and comparable to existing SNN alternatives on text, with substantially reduced parameter overhead.

papers.title: A non-randomized trial of the effects of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation on cognitive performance and resting state connectivity.
papers.summary: In a non-randomized trial of 40 healthy adults, active versus sham transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation was associated with improved BrainHQ cognitive-training performance and decreased frontal-central-parietal delta-band EEG connectivity, with delta connectivity during stimulation positively related to mood improvement; executive function tasks showed no group difference and effects did not survive multiple-comparison correction.

papers.title: Case Report: Electroencephalography-informed low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation targeting the supplementary motor area in severe functional movement disorder.
papers.summary: This case report describes a patient with severe functional movement disorder following an occupational injury who received EEG-informed low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation targeting the supplementary motor area followed by staged rehabilitation with visual feedback. The combined intervention reduced tremors and improved gait speed, activities of daily living, and EEG network connectivity.

papers.title: Effects of primary somatosensory cortex high-definition transcranial direct current stimulation combined with core stability training on pain and glutamate levels and neuromuscular function in chronic low back pain: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial of 36 adults with chronic low back pain, primary somatosensory cortex high-definition transcranial direct current stimulation combined with 4-week core stability training produced greater reductions in pain and disability scores versus sham. Active stimulation was also associated with decreased paraspinal muscle tone and stiffness, increased resting-state alpha power, reduced alpha phase-locking value connectivity, and lower circulating L-glutamate.

papers.title: Impaired brain reserve is associated with increased risk of overt hepatic encephalopathy occurrence in patients with cirrhosis.
papers.summary: In a retrospective analysis of a prospective cohort of 164 outpatients with cirrhosis, brain atrophy and impaired memory on the FCSRT were independently associated with overt hepatic encephalopathy occurrence during one-year follow-up, alongside prior overt hepatic encephalopathy, MELD score, and EEG background rhythm but not ammonia level. The authors conclude that impaired brain reserve is associated with increased risk of overt hepatic encephalopathy.

papers.title: Neurodevelopmental outcomes of infants evaluated for but not treated with therapeutic hypothermia: a prospective cohort study.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of infants evaluated for therapeutic hypothermia based on perinatal risk factors but not meeting institutional eligibility criteria, 13 of 26 infants completing Bayley-4 assessment (50%) showed sub-normative performance in at least one developmental domain at 24 months, despite only one having acute brain injury on MRI. Higher postnatal base deficits and lactate levels, and a trend toward less sleep-wake cycling on aEEG, were observed in those with sub-normative performance.

papers.title: Metabolic Imaging of Optic Nerve Oligodendrocytes Following AAV-Mediated Sensor Delivery.
papers.summary: This methods protocol describes intracerebroventricular adeno-associated virus injection at postnatal day 10 to express genetically encoded biosensors in optic nerve oligodendrocytes, enabling two-photon imaging of oligodendrocyte metabolism in intact white matter. A genetically encoded glucose sensor is demonstrated as a use case, with the approach compatible with functional assays such as optic nerve electrophysiology.

papers.title: Case Report: Sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease initially misdiagnosed as ischemic stroke: a diagnostic challenge and biomarker-based clarification.
papers.summary: Reports a 76-year-old man with CUL3-unrelated sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease initially misdiagnosed as ischemic stroke, clarified by progressive non-territorial cortical ribboning on MRI and markedly elevated CSF total tau, phosphorylated tau, and 14-3-3γ, meeting 2017 criteria for probable sCJD. The case highlights non-vascular diffusion patterns and CSF biomarkers as aids to diagnostic reconsideration.

papers.title: The History of Child Neurology in Iran: From Ancient Times to the Present.
papers.summary: Narrative historical review tracing child neurology in Iran from Persian-Islamic medical writings through Dar al-Funun reform, pediatric referral hospitals, and post-1985 integrated education to contemporary two-year subspecialty training, epilepsy monitoring, newborn screening, and neurogenetics resources such as Iranome. It identifies persistent challenges including uneven regional access, sanctions-related procurement barriers, and workforce migration.

papers.title: Reported Life-Threatening Polymorphic Ventricular Arrhythmia With Torsade-Like Morphology in a Patient With Gordon Syndrome and Hyperkalaemia.
papers.summary: Reports a 37-year-old woman with genetically confirmed CUL3-related Gordon syndrome who developed hyperkalaemia after a three-week interruption of bendroflumethiazide, with a reported self-terminating torsade-like polymorphic ventricular arrhythmia, and subsequently received an extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator after thiazide resumption improved potassium control. The authors note that the original rhythm tracing was unavailable and that the temporal association does not establish causation.

papers.title: Cre-loxP as an option in cardiovascular disease research.
papers.summary: Reviews the Cre-loxP site-specific recombination system for spatiotemporal control of gene expression in cardiovascular research, covering inducible promoter- and enhancer-driven Cre models that replicate human pathological conditions in mice and the use of Cre-loxP in optogenetics to express light-sensitive ion channels for studying cardiac electrophysiology.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
